scenes.title: Every agent keeps its own config
scenes.caption: Six agents, six places to change a provider or an MCP server.
scenes.narration: Claude, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode, VS Code. Each keeps its own settings, its own providers and its own list of tools.

scenes.title: Copying the files copies the keys
scenes.caption: The obvious fix carries your credentials with it.
scenes.narration: The obvious fix is to copy the files between machines. That can carry your API keys along with them.

scenes.title: CI Agent Sync
scenes.caption: A portable map for every agent, model, and mission.
scenes.narration: CI Agent Sync is a portable map for every agent. Provider routes, tool bundles and workflows live in one store you can read, version and review.

scenes.caption: A setup wizard on your own machine. Six steps, loopback only.
scenes.narration: It opens as a small web wizard on your own machine. Six steps, and it listens on loopback only.

shots.alt: The CI Agent Sync setup wizard, step one of six: 'Get every agent ready.' with the three-part setup path and a note that secrets, OAuth sessions, app databases and device identities stay out of the store.

before.eval: async () => { for (let i = 0; i < 100 && !document.querySelector('#loading-banner.loaded'); i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100)); if (!document.querySelector('#loading-banner.loaded')) throw new Error('stale stage: the store never loaded'); const n = document.querySelectorAll('#harness-options [data-agent]').length; if (n !== 11) throw new Error('stale stage: expected 11 harnesses, got ' + n); }

scenes.caption: Credential values live in 1Password. The wizard never asks you to paste one.
scenes.narration: Credential values stay in 1Password. The wizard hands you two commands to run, and never asks you to paste a key.

shots.alt: Step two, 'Connect your vault': two terminal commands for the 1Password setup and import, and a note that the wizard will not ask for a pasted credential.

scenes.caption: Eleven agents to choose from. Native sessions stay local.
scenes.narration: Pick the agents you use. Eleven are covered, from Claude and Codex to Hermes, OpenClaw and VS Code. Their sessions stay where they are.

shots.alt: Step three, 'Choose your agents': a list of the eleven harnesses, each with its capabilities, and the line 'Native sessions stay local.'

scenes.caption: A profile picks the reviewed bundles and the fallback order.
scenes.narration: Then a working profile: CEO, engineering or marketing. It picks the reviewed bundles and the fallback chain, and leaves native app state alone.

shots.alt: Step four, 'Pick a working profile': CEO, Engineering and Marketing, each with its bundles and default fallback chain, and the portable plan below.

scenes.caption: Generate writes to an ignored local folder. Your agents' own config is untouched.
scenes.narration: Generating the config writes into an ignored folder inside the store. It does not touch what your agents have installed.

shots.alt: Step four after pressing 'Generate portable config': the status line reads 'Portable artifacts generated under local/rendered.'

scenes.caption: A redacted backup first. Credential values and sessions are never copied.
scenes.narration: Before anything moves, it can take a redacted backup of the configs on the machine. Credential values and native sessions are never copied.

shots.alt: Step five, 'Back up before you go': the list of agent configs included in a redacted snapshot, with Preview backup and Create redacted backup buttons.

shots.alt: Step six, 'Your map is ready': the chosen profile and agent count, and the next commands, 'agentctl doctor --json' and 'agentctl sync'.

scenes.title: What travels, what stays
scenes.caption: Policy travels. Identity stays local. Every write crosses an approval boundary.
scenes.narration: Policy travels. Credentials stay in your vault, and sessions stay on each machine. Every write waits for your approval.
CI Agent Sync, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.
